title: Between an instant and a wall clock

blocks.text: An `Instant` is a point on the UTC timeline; a `LocalDateTime` is a reading of a wall clock, with no zone. Converting one into the other always needs a `ZoneId`: the same instant is a different wall-clock reading in each zone, and the same wall-clock reading is a different instant in each zone.

items: `static LocalDateTime localAt(Instant instant, ZoneId zone)` returns the date and time a wall clock in `zone` shows at `instant`.
`static Instant instantOf(LocalDateTime local, ZoneId zone)` returns the instant at which a wall clock in `zone` shows `local`.

cases.says: An instant reads as New York's and UTC's wall-clock time, and a UTC wall-clock time is the matching instant.
14:30 in New York and 14:30 in Tokyo are different instants.
18:30 UTC on March 15 is already 03:30 on March 16 in Tokyo.

concepts: Timestamps are stored as Instant and turned into a zone's wall-clock time only for display.
Converting between Instant and LocalDateTime always needs a zone, and the same wall-clock reading is a different instant in each zone.
